# ghp_secret_backend (Resource)

Mounts the ghp secrets engine and writes its connection config and service token. The engine checks the token against ghp on write, so a wrong URL or token fails the apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "ghp_admin_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "ghp_secret_backend" "ghp" {
  path        = "ghp"
  description = "Short-lived ghp tokens"
  base_url    = "https://ghp.example.com"
  admin_token = var.ghp_admin_token
  ca_cert     = file("${path.module}/ghp-ca.pem")

  request_timeout_seconds = 30
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `admin_token` (String, Sensitive) ghp service token (ghpsvc_...) the engine authenticates with. Write-only; never read back.
- `base_url` (String) Base URL of the ghp server, e.g. https://ghp.example.com.
- `path` (String) Mount path for the ghp secrets engine, e.g. "ghp". Changing it forces a new mount.

### Optional

- `ca_cert` (String, Sensitive) PEM CA certificate that signed the ghp server's TLS certificate. Write-only; never read back.
- `description` (String) Human-readable description of the mount. Defaults to "".
- `plugin` (String) Name of the plugin in the plugin catalog. Defaults to "vault-plugin-secrets-ghp".
- `request_timeout_seconds` (Number) HTTP timeout in seconds for calls from the plugin to ghp. Defaults to 30.
- `tls_skip_verify` (Boolean) Skip TLS verification of the ghp server (not recommended). Defaults to false.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Import by mount path. admin_token and ca_cert cannot be read back from Vault,
# so set them in configuration and run apply after importing.
terraform import ghp_secret_backend.ghp ghp
```
